issues.description: The problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice to be a static method (see the explicit note that calculateTotalPrice must be static), but the provided solution implements calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (public int calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon). This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about whether the method should be static and may lead to inconsistencies when comparing their implementation with the reference solution or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the reference implementation and the problem statement consistent. Either (A) update the solution so calculateTotalPrice is declared static (e.g., public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and adjust any internal usages accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement to remove the requirement that calculateTotalPrice be static and state that it should be an instance method. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem statement if the intention is to use a shared stock.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon 'stock' attribute in the constructor (it describes a final Stock stock that should be initialized to default values in the constructor), but it also later requires that the stock attribute be static (shared across instances). These two instructions conflict: a static field is not typically initialized per-instance in a constructor. The reference solution initializes the static stock at the declaration site (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This discrepancy between where and how the static stock should be initialized can confuse students about the intended design and where to place initialization.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to consistently describe the intended lifetime and initialization of the stock field. Either (A) require a non-static final Stock initialized in the constructor (and remove the static requirement), or (B) keep stock static and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor). Update the reference solution or the problem text accordingly so both match.
